title: SP-Kafka: Amazon MSK provisioned cluster, topics, consumer groups and dead-letter topics

sp.name: SP-Kafka
covers: Amazon MSK provisioned, Standard brokers (m5, m7g, t3.small)
Cluster: brokers, broker size, zones, storage and autoscaling, client authentication, TLS, configuration (unclean leader election, automatic topic creation, offset retention)
Topics as children: partitions, replication, min in-sync, retention, cleanup, message size, ordering, personal data, hot key
Consumer groups and a dead-letter topic per group by default (<topic>.<group>.dlq)
Load per broker (MB/s), partition replicas per broker, storage per broker, catch-up time after a consumer stop
Terraform: cluster, configuration, topics and dead-letter topics
not_covered: Apache Kafka in the data centre, Azure Event Hubs, Google Cloud Managed Kafka
Per-partition simulation over time (the rollup is per topic and broker)

integration.carries: Group, retries, dead-letter topic, idempotency, ordering, processing time

integration.means: Kafka has no HTTP entry point
integration.carries: Publish from a service, or add a REST proxy component

facts.label: Storage per broker
facts.note: Minimum 1 GiB, maximum 16384 GiB per broker.

facts.label: Wait between storage increases (manual or autoscaling)
facts.note: Storage can be increased, never decreased. The wait ranges from 6 hours to over 24 hours.

facts.label: Brokers per cluster (ZooKeeper-based)
facts.note: 60 for KRaft-based clusters; 90 brokers per account. Request more in Service Quotas.

facts.label: Default replication factor (3 zones)
facts.note: 2 for clusters in 2 zones.

facts.label: Default min.insync.replicas (3 zones)
facts.note: 1 for clusters in 2 zones.

facts.label: Unclean leader election, MSK default
facts.note: true on clusters without tiered storage, false with tiered storage. NEXUS generates a configuration that sets it to false.

facts.label: Automatic topic creation, MSK default
facts.note: false.

facts.label: Throughput per Standard broker
facts.note: AWS publishes no per-broker figure for Standard brokers; it points to the MSK sizing and pricing spreadsheet. NEXUS uses your organisation's measured ceilings (policy), none by default.

facts.label: Changing the broker size
facts.note: Rolling, one broker at a time; you can continue to produce and consume. Use 3 zones, replication factor 3 and min.insync.replicas at most RF − 1.

facts.label: Adding brokers
facts.note: Existing partitions stay where they are: rebalance by reassigning partitions to the new brokers (kafka-reassign-partitions.sh).

facts.label: Tiered storage
facts.note: Kafka 3.6.0 or higher (or 2.8.2.tiered), provisioned clusters only, not on kafka.t3.small.

facts.label: Encryption
facts.note: Always encrypted at rest (an AWS managed key if you choose none). In transit: TLS between brokers by default; client to broker TLS only by default (TLS 1.2).

facts.label: Client authentication
facts.note: IAM access control, mutual TLS or SASL/SCRAM; unauthenticated access can be enabled.

rules.rationale: Brokers over at least two zones, the count a multiple of the zones.
rules.fix: Use the next multiple of the zones.

rules.rationale: Replication factor 3 and min in-sync 2 keep writes and data through one broker loss.
Unclean leader election can silently lose acknowledged messages.
Too many partition replicas per broker slow the cluster and block updates.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: add brokers, a larger size or fewer partitions.

rules.rationale: Traffic per broker within the organisation's measured ceiling, with headroom.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: add brokers or a larger size.

rules.rationale: Storage per broker must hold the retention for every copy.
Retention must outlast the longest planned consumer outage.
rules.fix: Keep messages for the policy's planned outage.

rules.rationale: Committed positions must outlast the longest planned consumer outage.
After a short stop, a group must catch up within the RTO.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: add consumers and partitions, or process faster.

rules.rationale: acks=all and the idempotent producer for business events.
rules.fix: Use acks=all with the idempotent producer.

rules.rationale: Kafka delivers at least once; consumers must deduplicate.
Every consumer group has a dead-letter topic by default.
Failed messages kept long enough to investigate and redrive.
Ordered topics stop the partition instead of skipping messages.
Ordered topics need a key so one entity's events stay in one partition.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: choose the entity id as the key.

rules.rationale: Within a group each partition has one consumer; extra consumers idle.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: add partitions or fewer consumers.

rules.rationale: One key with a large share of traffic makes one partition the bottleneck.
rules.fix: No automatic fix: re-key or split the hot key.

rules.rationale: Clients authenticate and traffic is encrypted.
Topics are created as code, not by a typo in a producer.
Personal data in streams is kept only as long as policy allows.
A service that writes its database and publishes uses an outbox.
